solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fool plugs openings of mortars in firing range

indicators.note: something that plugs a gap sits inside it, so one word goes into the other
openings are beginnings, so only the first letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: first letters of the three words
a fool is an ass

explanation.surface: A clumsy soldier jams the mouths of mortars on an artillery range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like part of the military scene, but it is the definition: a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, so it is a kind of mountain range.

clue.text: Little boy, one month old, shows a certain style

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur
Dec is the abbreviation for December
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A small boy aged one month is already displaying his own look.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s, so it is one particular style.

clue.text: Jolly insult wraps up stellar transmission

indicators.note: to wrap something up is to enclose it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a slight is an insult
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, and a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A cheerful insult somehow concludes a broadcast from space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' reads as an adjective but is a noun: old naval slang for a marine, here standing in for any sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlight is the light emitted by stars, which is literally a transmission from a stellar source.

clue.text: Abandon benefit cuts — really?!

indicators.note: a word that cuts into another sits inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: to forsake is to abandon
goodness is the benefit or nourishment in something

explanation.surface: An exasperated reaction to news that welfare payments are being slashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of exasperated disbelief, used when someone can hardly credit what they hear.

clue.text: Monk toils with spades in mine

parts.note: toils are snares or nets, so a trap

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A monk labours underground with shovels in a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toils' looks like a verb for labour but is the noun meaning snares. The setter of this puzzle is Monk, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a member of a strict Cistercian order of monks known for silence.

clue.text: There's no danger Carol will be upset with 15

indicators.note: upset things are knocked into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 15 across

explanation.surface: Reassuring someone that nothing bad will happen if Carol gets annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says nobody is watching or in the way, so it is safe to proceed without danger.

clue.text: Mason has found tiny hollow cracks for quite some time

indicators.note: something that cracks breaks apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its middle scooped out, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A stonemason has discovered a small cavity that has been splitting the stone for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very long time, as long as thirty Sundays strung together.

clue.text: Trace of paint, very dark reddish

indicators.note: a trace is only a tiny bit, so just the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter
inky means very dark, black as ink

explanation.surface: A smear of paint with a deep, dark red-brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinky describes a colour tinged with pink, which is a pale shade of red.

clue.text: Turn up to stop despicable sort, having no time for miser

indicators.note: something that stops a hole plugs it, so it sits inside
having none of something means it is taken away, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: scrote is British slang for a contemptible person
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Someone shows up to block a nasty character, swapping time for a tight-fisted man.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrote is a British slang insult for a worthless lout.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge from Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the archetypal miser, so his name stands for any stingy person.

clue.text: Fractious teen let slip line "I'll do what I like"

indicators.note: letters that are let slip escape from their order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A grumpy teenager blurts out a defiant phrase claiming the right to do as they please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fractious' looks like a description of the teen, but it is fodder: its letters go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock retort asserts personal liberty, a declaration that the speaker may act as they please.

clue.text: Rich bore wants fuss

parts.note: a bore is a borehole, such as a well
a to-do is a fuss

explanation.surface: A wealthy but tedious person demands a fuss be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests a dull person, but it is a hole drilled for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means prosperous or wealthy, a synonym for rich.

clue.text: With-it younger man?

parts.note: surface reading: a fashionable, trendy young man; setter's reading: 'it' is sex appeal, and a young male lover kept as a plaything has it

explanation.walkthrough: 'With-it' looks like 'trendy', but 'it' is the old slang for sex appeal; the answer is the young lover of an older woman, kept like a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy boy is a much younger male lover of an older woman, who is valued for his youthful appeal.

clue.text: Perhaps crack pipe from back of cistern in loo

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A drug pipe has turned up behind the toilet cistern.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a lavatory. 'Perhaps' signals that crack pipe is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bong is a water pipe for smoking drugs, so a crack pipe is one possible example.

clue.text: Put out pet found in badly soiled end of bed

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it
things done badly come out wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: last letter
a cat is a typical pet

explanation.surface: The family pet was turfed out after being discovered on a dirty end of the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as evicting the pet, but it means a joint knocked out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: A dislocated joint has been put out of its socket, so the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Overbearing mule runs into sea loch

parts.note: a mule is close kin to an ass, and both mean a stubborn fool

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it

parts.note: Loch Etive is a sea loch in western Scotland
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A bossy mule charges into a Scottish sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea loch is a Scottish inlet of the sea; Loch Etive is a well-known one in Argyll.
explanation.definitionFit: Assertive means forcefully confident, which shades into domineering behaviour, so overbearing is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Philosophy of Art teaches its faults

indicators.note: faults are geological fractures, so the letters are broken up and shifted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosophy of art lecturer teaches its shortcomings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faults' reads as a noun meaning flaws, but works as the signal to rearrange, like rock shifting along a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetics is the branch of philosophy that studies beauty and taste in art.

clue.text: Strict unopened message concerning the setter

indicators.note: something unopened lacks its opening, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
re means concerning, about
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A severe letter about the compiler that nobody has opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme measures are severe and uncompromising, so extreme can mean strict in its harshest form.

clue.text: Front of seasoned wood window frame

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter
ash is a type of wood

explanation.surface: The front window frame is made of seasoned timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass panes in a sash window.

clue.text: Way to classify rum

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to range things is to arrange or class them

explanation.surface: A method for sorting rums by type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but it is the British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is informal British for odd or peculiar, a synonym of strange.

clue.text: Flight from Ireland checked by curt secret police

indicators.note: something checked by another is held in, so it sits inside
curt means short, so the word is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: the Stasi was the East German secret police
IR is an abbreviation for Ireland

explanation.surface: An escape from Ireland is halted by brusque secret police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests fleeing the country, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, so stairs is a synonym.

clue.text: Stroke, cut wildly, is making the boundary

indicators.note: the boundary goes around the outside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: done wildly means done in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman's wild cut shot reaches the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (a cut is a shot, a boundary scores four) hides a medical or poetic term.
explanation.definitionFit: An ictus is a stroke or seizure in medicine, and also the stress beat in verse.

clue.text: Perverse hoax heralds delay, article appearing late

indicators.note: the article is moved to turn up later in the word than it was
something that heralds comes in front of what follows

parts.note: a con is a trick or hoax
to tarry is to delay
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A contrary prank precedes a hold-up, with a newspaper piece published late.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in the word for delay is shifted one place further back.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary means deliberately opposite or awkward, which is what perverse means.

clue.text: Stewed pears nauseating for some senior citizens

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down into a mess, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stewed pears served in a care home are revolting to the elderly residents.
explanation.definitionFit: Septuagenarians are people in their seventies, so they are some, not all, of the elderly.

clue.text: Chaps say "shit", maybe, when eg "shirt" is required

parts.note: chaps are men
saying a rude word is to swear

explanation.surface: Men curse when they type a word missing its R and it comes out rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: shit plus R is shirt, so 'swear' and 'wear' are one R apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt is an example of clothing for men, so it is required for a men's clothing department.

clue.text: Drain blocked by the ultimate in thick spit

indicators.note: a pipe blocked by something has it lodged inside

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A drain clogged with dense spittle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' looks like saliva but is the rod for roasting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a long rod pushed through meat for roasting, which is a kind of skewer.
